Mandatory rules:
- Do NOT write replacement section content.

SECTION: unify_bullets

RUBRIC_REF: apps_rg/runtime/judges/employment_bullet_judge_rubric.py#unify_bullets

You are evaluating exactly 6 employment bullets (bul_unify_001..006).
This is a BULLET-LINE lane — not an executive summary paragraph.
Return JSON only with: score_scale, score, threshold, pass, decisive_failure, findings, cited_sentence_indexes, remediation_suggestions.

Score contract:
- score_scale must be "0_to_1" or "0_to_5" only.
- Keep score and threshold within the declared scale.
- Employment pool lanes: min_selection_score is the pass floor for Claude pool selection.

Rubric dimensions (employment bullets — not executive summary):
1. claim_ledger_grounding: each bullet maps to bul_* source_fact_ids in the claim ledger; metrics match allowed facts verbatim.
2. bullet_line_discipline: one high-impact resume bullet per slot — concise line, no narrative paragraph or multi-sentence block.
3. jd_briefing_targeting_discipline: JD and briefing shape emphasis only — never JD-as-proof, briefing-as-proof, or target company as experience.
4. keyword_discipline_without_stuffing: role-relevant phrasing without ATS keyword bags or copied JD phrases as proof.
5. cross_bullet_outcome_diversity: each bullet answers a distinct outcome spine — not six restatements of the same mechanism stack.
6. employer_scope_purity: no cross-employer fact leakage, wrong-company names, or facts from other employment slices.
7. current_role_unify_platform_signal: Unify reads as the candidate's current-role platform proof (governance, commercialization, scale) where evidenced.
8. protected_metric_anchor: bul_unify_006 preserves locked commercial metrics ($22M / margin / team scale) and approved metric_outcome_id anchors without splitting or diluting.
9. mechanism_inventory_cap: at most one mechanism-dense bullet; others stay outcome-led, not comma-stacked architecture inventories.

Decisive failure triggers:
- unsupported metric or cross-employer fact leakage (IBM/InsurTech/EY)
- first-person language
- wrong bullet count (expected 6)
- protected bul_unify_006 metrics missing or split incorrectly
- JD phrase copied as proof (>4 consecutive words)
- generic filler that loses Unify-specific mechanisms or protected metrics

Return ONLY one compact JSON object:
{"score_scale":"0_to_5","score":0.0,"threshold":4.0,"pass":true,"decisive_failure":false,
 "findings":["short strings"],"cited_sentence_indexes":[1],
 "remediation_suggestions":[],"rationale":"one short paragraph",
 "fail_reasons":[],"unsupported_claims":[],"quality_flags":[]}
score_scale must be 0_to_5 or 0_to_1 with in-range score/threshold.

{
  "target_title": "Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships",
  "target_company": "Anthropic",
  "jd_text": "Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships\nSan Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA\n\nAbout Anthropic\n\nAnthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.\n\nAbout the role\n\nAs the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.\n\nYou will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.\n\nResponsibilities\n\n    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.\n    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.\n    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.\n    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.\n    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.\n    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.\n\nYou may be a good fit if you have\n\n    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).\n    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.\n    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).\n    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.\n    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.\n    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.\n    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.\n\nStrong candidates may also have\n\n    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.\n    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.\n\nCompensation\n\nThe annual compensation range for this role is listed below.\n\nFor sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings (\"OTE\") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.\n\nAnnual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD",
  "briefing": "# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet\n| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 OTE | Reports to Partnerships / GTM leadership (partner-led enterprise adoption) |\n\n## JD Complement\nThis is not simply a technical-management hire. Anthropic is formalizing the layer between frontier-model capability and repeatable enterprise implementation through external delivery organizations.\n\nThe operating tension is scale versus control: partners can multiply reach and implementation capacity, but Anthropic must preserve product quality, security expectations, responsible-use standards, and a coherent customer experience across\ndeployments it does not directly deliver.\n\n## Company DNA & Operating Model\nAnthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation and AI safety and research company. Its commercial identity is a hybrid of frontier-model provider, developer platform, and enterprise software vendor.\n\nIts dominant enterprise motion increasingly depends on putting Claude into customer workflows through multiple routes: Claude for Enterprise, the Claude platform, API-based applications, and managed agent infrastructure.\n\nThe company’s differentiation is tied to reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. That makes implementation architecture a commercial and governance issue, not only a pre-sales exercise: partners need to create useful solutions\nwithout misrepresenting model behavior or bypassing responsible deployment practices.\n\n## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure\nAnthropic is converting a research-led model business into an enterprise adoption system. That transition creates pressure to make successful deployments more repeatable across business teams, developers, and large implementation partners.\n\nClaude for Enterprise is positioned around security, compliance, and business/developer use cases. Anthropic’s own enterprise deployment materials frame adoption as a four-phase process spanning technical setup, change management and\nlaunch, rather than a standalone software activation.\n\nThe decision-rights tension is likely between central product and engineering teams, which own core platform behavior, and field or partner teams, which see deployment friction first. The valuable operating mechanism is a disciplined\nfeedback loop that turns recurring implementation patterns into enablement, product inputs, and reusable architectures.\n\n## Leadership & Stakeholder Map\nAnthropic was founded by former OpenAI researchers, including Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei. Its public identity continues to combine research, safety, policy, engineering, and commercial work.\n\nRelevant stakeholder groups include:\n- Partnerships and GTM leaders shaping cloud, services, and technology-partner coverage.\n- Product and engineering teams responsible for Claude products, API capabilities, and managed agent infrastructure.\n- Enterprise and developer-facing teams responsible for secure adoption and implementation experience.\n- Safety, policy, and responsible-use functions whose standards affect partner solution design and customer deployment boundaries.\n- Cloud, technology, and services partners that extend market access and delivery capacity.\n\n## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals\nAnthropic operates both an enterprise application surface and a developer platform. The Claude platform is positioned for creating agents and applications with frontier Claude models and managed agent infrastructure.\n\nThat architecture creates a practical divide that partner teams must bridge: business-user deployments, custom API integrations, and agentic applications may share a model provider but demand different governance, implementation, and\nsupport patterns.\n\nClaude Enterprise’s emphasis on security and compliance makes enterprise architecture conversations likely to include administrative controls, deployment readiness, adoption design, and operational ownership—not only prompts or model\nselection.\n\nAnthropic’s research positioning around reliability, interpretability, and steerability is material to solution design. Partners need patterns that translate those product principles into customer-facing use cases and deployment guardrails.\n\n## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion\nPartnership is material to Anthropic’s commercial model. Anthropic publicly describes a network of cloud, technology, and services partners intended to help customers address AI challenges.\n\nThe ecosystem motion is broader than referral selling:\n- Cloud partners provide infrastructure, routes to market, and technical distribution.\n- Services partners provide implementation capacity, change-management support, and industry context.\n- Technology partners can embed or extend Claude within customer technology stacks.\n- Enterprise deployment requires co-ordinated technical enablement, not just commercial account mapping.\n\nAccenture publicly positions its Anthropic relationship around enterprise AI deployment, productivity, value creation, and new-product development. This signals a joint-solution and delivery-oriented model in which partners need credible\narchitectures, implementation methods, and escalation paths.\n\nThe central partnership challenge is to let partners lead enough of the customer journey to scale adoption while keeping Anthropic close enough to strategic technical decisions, product feedback, and implementation quality.\n\n## Recent Events & Urgency\nAnthropic’s public platform now emphasizes managed agent infrastructure alongside frontier Claude models. This raises the implementation bar for partners: customer conversations can move from isolated AI use cases toward more durable\napplications and agent workflows.\n\nThe company has also made enterprise deployment guidance and adoption education publicly available. That indicates an effort to operationalize implementation knowledge rather than leave adoption entirely to bespoke field support.\n\nAs enterprise AI buyers move from experimentation to governed deployment, Anthropic faces pressure to make partner-delivered outcomes repeatable across security-conscious organizations while preserving its safety-centered brand.\n\n## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)\n- Building partner technical motions that convert platform capability into repeatable customer deployments.\n- Scaling GSI, cloud, and technology-partner enablement without diluting architecture standards.\n- Creating reference architectures and field feedback loops for API, enterprise, and agentic use cases.\n- Leading technical teams across product, engineering, sales, and partner stakeholders.\n- Treating enterprise adoption as technical setup plus governance, change management, and operating ownership.\n- Balancing ecosystem velocity with responsible-AI, security, and customer-trust requirements.\n- Supporting strategic deals while codifying reusable patterns that reduce dependency on bespoke intervention.\n\n## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)\n- Anthropic’s partner ecosystem spans cloud, technology, and services providers rather than a single-channel model.\n- Claude adoption appears to require both technical implementation and organizational change management.\n- The managed-agent platform direction increases the need for production-grade partner architecture patterns.\n- Accenture’s public Anthropic deployment positioning makes joint delivery quality a visible ecosystem issue.\n- A safety-centered company faces a distinct challenge in scaling third-party implementation without losing consistency.\n- The most interesting partnership question is how Anthropic turns deployment learnings into better enablement and product decisions.\n\n## Do Not Use As Proof\nThe JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, outcomes, scope, leadership experience, technical depth, and partnership results must come from the governed resume/proof graph."

You are a strict executive resume judge. Output a single compact JSON object only. No markdown fences, no explanatory prose, no nested finding objects.

GRADE_ONLY authority (all providers — Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic):
- Do NOT rewrite, replace, or edit candidate_output.resume_display_text.
- deterministic_gate_summary is authoritative: if a gate shows "pass": true, do NOT fail or cite that axis.
- Do NOT apply retired SRFS slot mandates as decisive failures: five-part S1–S5 arc, mandatory S5 credibility
  sentence, S2 mechanism-only / S4 outcomes slot shapes, srfs_sentence_responsibility.
- When x2_exec_summary_evidence_utilization.pass is true, unused_fact_ids are optional weave targets, not defects.

Return ONLY one compact JSON object. No markdown fences, no prose before or after, no nested objects.
Required shape (findings and remediation_suggestions must be arrays of short strings only):
{"score_scale":"0_to_5","score":0.0,"threshold":4.0,"pass":true,"decisive_failure":false,"findings":["..."],"cited_sentence_indexes":[1],"remediation_suggestions":[],"dimension_verdicts":{...8 rubric keys...}}
At most 6 short strings in findings and 4 in remediation_suggestions.
cited_sentence_indexes: 1-based indexes (S1=1 … S6=6) for every sentence your findings ask to change.
Include dimension_verdicts with all eight rubric dimension ids (pass/severity/codes per dimension).

Score contract (mandatory - every judge response MUST comply):
- Include score_scale as exactly one of: "0_to_1" or "0_to_5". Do not omit score_scale.
- If score_scale is "0_to_1": score and threshold MUST each be a number from 0.0 through 1.0 inclusive.
- If score_scale is "0_to_5": score and threshold MUST each be a number from 0.0 through 5.0 inclusive.
- Forbidden: 0_to_10 scales, percentage scores (0–100), or values like score=9.2 with threshold=8.0.
- Do not infer scale from magnitude; declare score_scale explicitly and keep score/threshold within that scale.
